title: The Quran and the Mosque
welcome_lead: Open the Quran and step inside the mosque to discover the heart of Islamic life.
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on the Quran and the role of the mosque in Islam.
final_note: You can now describe the Quran and what happens in a mosque.

walkthroughs.body_html: Muslims believe the Quran is the word of Allah, revealed to Muhammad over 23 years through the angel Jibril. It has 114 chapters called Surahs. Muslims read it in Arabic, and many memorise large parts or all of it.

A mosque has a large open prayer hall with no chairs — people pray on mats. A niche (mihrab) shows the direction of Mecca (qibla). The mosque often has a dome and one or more minarets. Shoes are removed before entering, and worshippers wash first.
The most important prayer of the week is Jumu'ah, held at the mosque around midday on Fridays. The imam gives a sermon (khutbah) and leads the congregation in prayer.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: Atonement means Jesus apologised to humans for being born divine.
It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
